resources.string: "That was your free time. Here's what it showed."
"Your talks were too short to make questions from. Your report goes on without it."
"A few minutes, made from what you said: the words, the phrases, the corrections."
"It moves as you talk. Progress keeps track."
"A few more talks and your level is ready."
"You can change all of it later in My routine."
"We went through every minute of your free time and put this together just for you."
"From now on, every week's study comes to you as a report like this."
"A first read, from %d min of you speaking. It gets sharper as you talk."
"Read from %d min of you speaking. It moves as you talk, and Progress keeps track."
"You also spoke %1$s (%2$d min). This report reads one language at a time."
"Two quick questions, and anything you want to tell us. We read every one."
"Time that didn't go to scrolling. Well spent."
"You only talked. Talking makes you quicker, but a correction only sticks once you say it right yourself. After a call, run Say it again, and clear a few review cards a day."
"Talking is the heart of it. Everything else is built from your calls."
"You tried most of it. That mix is what makes it stick."
"Add Say it again next. It runs your last talk again with your lines corrected, and that's where the fixes stick."
"Add a few review cards a day. The words and corrections from your talks come back until they're yours."
"Add shadowing next. Saying the fluent lines in your own voice trains the rhythm talking alone doesn't."
"Try a scene next. Watch a situation you're about to face played out, then talk it through."
"Try listening next. A few minutes on the go keeps your ear in the language between calls."
"Try a speech next. One recorded take shows how you sound when you have to keep going on your own."
"Redo a talk with your lines corrected"
"Say the fluent lines in your own voice"
"Record a speech and get a score"
